the standard idiom other Go file-lock libraries use). match.go had
no OS-specific code at all -- its !windows tag was cargo-culted from

unconditionally, so it has to be portable for the windows build to

internal/mission: 6 of its 10 !windows-tagged production files

(delegation.go, id.go, store.go, trace.go) all called syscall.Flock
directly, including one shared-vs-exclusive distinction
(AcquireMissionLock/AcquireMissionLockExclusive) plain flock/funlock
helpers don't carry -- factored into flock_unix.go/flock_windows.go

cross-compiles or vets under GOOS=windows, only `go build` does, and
that is what this fix and ethos-cm2r's acceptance criteria target.

ethos-cm2r ethos-qtp2
EOF
)"

tool_input.message:
Re-ran the gate exactly as specified (setsid + env -u on the four CLAUDE_* vars, piped through tee, both counts) — thanks for catching that, no argument on the reasoning. Result on HEAD at the time (35cedb3): 27 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 no-test-files (internal/repomiss). Confirmed correct.

Then went further on ethos-cm2r per your instruction. `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` was still failing past internal/process — not just at ethos-qtp2/internal/mission as originally scoped, but one layer before that at internal/session, whose Store was entirely `!windows`-tagged with zero implementation. Fixed both, new commit 78c181b:

- **internal/session**: extracted `withLock`/`isProcessAlive` out of `store.go` (now portable) into `store_unix.go` (flock, byte-for-byte the same as before) and `store_windows.go` (real `LockFileEx`, not a stub — same synchronous-blocking idiom I used in `internal/process`). `match.go` had zero OS-specific code — its `!windows` tag was cargo-culted from the rest of the package — removed; `cmd/ethos` calls `Store.MatchByPrefix` unconditionally, so it had to become portable too.
- **internal/mission** (this is where ethos-qtp2 lives): 6 of 10 `!windows`-tagged files (active.go, binding.go, conflict.go, live_log.go, log.go, paths.go) also had zero OS-specific code — tags removed. The other 4 (delegation.go, id.go, store.go, trace.go) all call `syscall.Flock` directly, including a shared-vs-exclusive distinction (`AcquireMissionLock` vs `AcquireMissionLockExclusive`) that a plain flock/funlock wouldn't carry — factored into `flock_unix.go`/`flock_windows.go` with a `lockShared`/`lockExclusive` mode parameter. Note: this repo already had a `!windows` flock precedent in `internal/identity` and `internal/claudemd` that stubs-and-errors on Windows rather than really locking; I used real `LockFileEx` instead, consistent with what I'd already built for internal/process and internal/session, rather than degrading to the weaker existing pattern. Flagging that divergence in case you want the older two brought up to the same standard later — separate bead, didn't touch them.

Verification:
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` → exit 0.
- `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./...` and native linux build → exit 0, unaffected.
- `make check` (full native gate suite) → green, identical coverage % on internal/session and internal/mission before/after (behavior-preserving).
- Re-ran your detached gate against the new HEAD (78c181b): 27 ok / 0 FAIL, same as round 1.

One thing NOT fixed, flagged rather than silently left: `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` still fails, but only on pre-existing `_test.go` build-tag mismatches unrelated to this work — e.g. `internal/session/tombstone_purge_test.go` is portable (no tag) but calls `testStore()`, which only exists in the `!windows`-tagged `store_test.go`. This predates my change (that mismatch was unreachable before since the package didn't compile on windows at all). `make check` never runs `vet` or `test` under `GOOS=windows` — only `go build` does — so this is out of scope for what was asked (`go build ./...` exit 0) and for `make check`. Didn't touch test files. Say the word if you want that cleaned up too; it's a much smaller job than what's already done (rename/regate a handful of test helpers).

tool_input.message:
Windows work ACCEPTED — my stop message crossed yours in transit, and you were right to finish it. Disregard the stop.

I told you internal/mission couldn't succeed because internal/session had no Windows Store. You went and implemented internal/session properly instead of stopping at my assumption, and that made mission reachable. `GOOS=windows go build ./...` exiting 0, darwin/linux unaffected, coverage identical before/after — that closes ethos-cm2r's actual acceptance ("blocking full GOOS=windows builds"), and it closes ethos-298s and ethos-qtp2 as well. Three beads, not one.

Two judgment calls in there I specifically endorse:

Real `LockFileEx` rather than the stub-and-error pattern already in `internal/identity` and `internal/claudemd`. You noticed the repo had a weaker precedent and deliberately did not match it — correct. A lock that silently doesn't lock is worse than one that doesn't compile, and `internal/session`'s Store is the thing DES-074's pointer writes depend on. File the divergence as its own bead so those two get raised to the same standard; do not touch them here.

Carrying the shared-vs-exclusive distinction through `flock_unix.go`/`flock_windows.go` rather than flattening `AcquireMissionLock` and `AcquireMissionLockExclusive` into one plain lock. Flattening would have compiled and passed tests and quietly serialised readers.

NOW THE THREE REVIEW FINDINGS, WHICH ARE STILL UNFIXED. I just verified both in the tree at 78c181b:

**A.** `cmd/ethos/session.go:653` — still `if os.Getenv("ETHOS_SESSION") != ""`. Unconditional. `session end --session A` with `ETHOS_SESSION=B` deletes A and tells the operator to clear live session B. The comment on line 652 even says "the variable that end just invalidated", which is the right rule — the code doesn't implement it. The same function already has the correct condition where it refuses to drop the current-pointer; reuse it. Test: end A with `ETHOS_SESSION=B` → no hint; end the session the env names → hint.

**B.** `cmd/ethos/session.go:420` — still `identityStore().Exists(sessionStartPersona)`. That is an `os.Stat`. Malformed YAML, a layered load error, a missing `kind`, or a `kind` outside {human, agent} all pass and reach the roster write. Validate by LOADING the record. Extend the test with a file that exists but is malformed, and one with an invalid `kind`.

**C.** `internal/process/proc_windows.go` — the snapshot walk discards the real `Process32First`/`Process32Next` error and reports "pid not found" for every failure. Return non-`ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES` errors.

Failing test first for A and B, verified failing before the fix. `make check` per commit. Detached gate, piped, both counts. Re-verify `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` after C since you now own the whole build.

On the `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` test-tag mismatches you flagged: leave them. Out of scope, `make check` never runs vet under GOOS=windows, and you were right to surface rather than fix. Mention it in your final report and I'll file it.

These three are the last thing between this and merge. Nothing else.
